previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and recent cystectomy with urostomy presented with two days of sharp lower abdominal and back pain. He was afebrile and hemodynamically stable. Evaluation revealed an interval increase in ascites and left ureterohydronephrosis on CT imaging, along with urinalysis findings suggestive of infection despite no fever or flank tenderness. He was treated with antibiotics and monitored for pyelonephritis. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home the same day with instructions to follow up with urology and primary care. Additional support was arranged for urostomy bag management due to reported difficulties with adhesion.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ yo man with a history of HCV, etOH Cirrhosis 
w/ grade I varices/PHG, ascites, bladder/prostate Ca s/p 
resection and ileal conduit (___), CAD s/p MI, CKDIII, 
multiple admissions for hematuria who presents with fall, 
weakness, and recurrent hematuria. 

#Fall: Patient reports feeling lightheaded and having his legs 
give out while outside home ___ day following ___ discharge. 
CT spine (c-spine and torso) showed no fracture & he was 
ambulating without difficulty during hospitalization. Fall 
thought to be combination of etOH given etOH level 96 on 
admission in combination with possible orthostasis and anemia. 
No arrhythmias noted on telemetry during admission. Pt refused 
orthostatic vital signs. TSH wnl and B12 elevated. He had a left 
sided facial droop and left sided weakness concerning for 
possible sub acute stroke. Neurology recommended a non emergent 
MRI. He also described symptoms concerning for seizure including 
facial pulling for which he was started on EEG which was stopped 
early because he decided to leave against medical advice. 
Initial EEG read was without epileptiform activity. 

#Toxometabolic Encephalopathy: Patient initially presented to 
the ED after fall as above, felt to be in the setting of alcohol 
intoxication as above. He was uncooperative and agitated in ED 
but was alert and arousable. Patient was pancultured but was 
afebrile and not meeting SIRS criteria to suggest infection as 
the etiology of his encephalopathy. Given ongoing etOH abuse, he 
was placed on CIWA but did not require lorazepam during his 
stay. He was alert and oriented on the day of discharge.  

#Hematuria: Patient has had frequent presentations for 
hematuria, most recently ___ at ___. In review, he has had 
extensive workup in the past and has been seen by GI, urology, 
and ___ with consensus that recurrent bleeding is unlikely due to 
variceal bleed and that there is no role for TIPS or ___ 
procedure. Per note from ___, urology at ___ suspects bleeding 
___ high venous pressures from cirrhosis and via normal 
sloughing of ileal mucosal surface vs local irritation + 
episodic engorged vein unroofs and rebleeds. Pt not a surgical 
candidate for stoma revision. Periodically has had suture placed 
(recently on ___ in ED due to observed mucosal bleed of stoma 
(not surrounding skin)) but previously has declined to cauterize 
stomal bleeding site. After changing his urostomy bag, he 
continued to drain clear yellow urine from both urostomy and 
PCN. Currently PCN and urostomy draining yellow urine. 

#Anemia: Admission His H/H was ___ and he was given 1uPRB 
with improvement to 8.4/26. Pt has chronic blood loss for which 
he has had extensive workup in the past as above given concern 
for hematuria as the source. Fe studies have shown ACD with 
cirrhosis. 

#Alcohol Abuse: Long history of alcohol abuse complicated by 
alcoholic cirrhosis presents with a EtOH of 96 in ED.
- maintain on CIWA w/lorazepam for >10 as above
- social work consult
- nutrition consult

#Pyuria: UA from urostomy shows WBC, moderate bacteria; recent 
UCx from ___ shows mixed bacterial flora. No antibiotics given 
no leukocytosis, fever, or other evidence of infection. Urine 
culture pending at discharge.

#Disposition: On ___, patient threatened to leave against 
medical advice. Medical team attempted to compromise with 
patient and he initially agreed to wait for CBC, abdominal US 
and EEG final results before leaving. Around 12 ___, he 
unfortunately walked off of the floor and eloped. 

Chronic:
#Bladder, prostate cancer: s/p resection and ilioconduit ___, no radiation, no chemo. Patient's home urostomy bag was 
changed this admission. F/u with urologist ___ ___. 

#Cirrhosis: MELD 13, Childs ___ B, secondary to etOH and HCV. 
Transplant status: not candidate given ongoing etOH abuse. 
Variceal status: last EGD ___ with grade I varices, patient 
was on home nadolol which was held in the setting ___ this 
admission. Ascites: most recent U/S ___ at ___ showed small 
ascites but not significant for paracentesis. Ascites controlled 
with Lasix/spironolactone. Abd U/S this admission showed no 
ascites. Hepatic encephalopathy: not currently on 
lactulose/rifaximin at home. No asterixis to suggest HE at this 
time and so not initiated this admission. ___ screen: next 
screen due ___ per ___ records. Patient to continue follow 
up with hepatology at ___. 

#Hydronephrosis: patient has left PCN, placed in ___ at ___ 
due to left hydronephrosis seen on imaging. As above, he was not 
empirically treated for his pyuria as above. Nephrostomy 
continued to drain clear yellow urine. 

#HTN: held home Lisinopril in setting ___ during admission. 

#GERD: continued home omeprazole

FINDINGS: 

Liver:  The hepatic parenchyma is coarsened.   No focal liver lesions are
identified.  There is no ascites.
Bile ducts:  There is no intrahepatic biliary ductal dilation.  The common
hepatic duct measures 2 mm.
Gallbladder:  The gallbladder is decompressed.
Pancreas:  The imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits,
with portions of the pancreatic tail obscured by overlying bowel gas.
Spleen:  The spleen demonstrates normal echotexture, and measures 13.5 cm.
Kidneys:  The right kidney measures 10.2 cm.  The left kidney measures 10.3
cm.  Echogenic material seen within the left kidney is felt to reflect known
percutaneous nephrostomy catheter.  Visualized portions of the left kidney
show mild left hydroureteronephrosis.  There is no hydronephrosis in the right
kidney.

Doppler evaluation:

The main portal vein is patent, with flow in the appropriate direction.
Main portal vein velocity is 9.8 cm/sec.
The posterior branch of the right portal vein is patent with antegrade flow. 
The right portal vein and anterior branch of the right portal vein were not
visualized.  The left portal vein is patent with reversal of flow.

The main hepatic artery is patent, with appropriate waveform.
Right, middle and left hepatic veins are patent, with appropriate waveforms.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Patent hepatic vasculature.  Reversal of flow in the left portal
vein.Right portal vein and anterior branch of the right portal vein were not
visualized.
2. No ascites.
3.  Splenomegaly.
4. Mild left hydroureteronephrosis.
